label: Dentist visit

what_happens.title: What happens at the dentist
goals: The steps of a check-up, in order
The chair, the lamp and counting teeth are normal
what_happens.parentSkill: Describe the visit step by step, in plain words, without promises about how it will feel.

who_is_there.title: Who is at the dentist
goals: Meet the desk person, the hygienist and the dentist
Masks and gloves are normal and friendly
who_is_there.parentSkill: Name the new people ahead of time, so strangers become 'the helper I already know about'.

what_i_do.title: My job in the big chair
goals: Sit, open wide, keep still for a short time
The sounds, tastes and light of the tools
what_i_do.parentSkill: Give your child a job: a clear action turns a scary place into something they do, not something done to them.

if_scared.title: If I feel worried
goals: Honest: it may pinch, press or tickle, and it is quick
A stop signal: raise a hand
Ways to feel calm: squeeze, breathe
if_scared.parentSkill: Validate the feeling first ('It's okay to feel worried'), then offer one coping tool. Avoid 'it won't hurt'.

rehearsal.title: Let's play dentist
goals: Practise the visit at home through play
The end: sticker, praise, going home together
rehearsal.parentSkill: Rehearse through play: let your child be the dentist too, so they hold some control.

steps: Walk into the clinic and check in at the desk
Sit in the big chair; it moves up and the lamp turns on
The dentist counts and checks teeth with a small mirror
Pick a sticker and go home
sensory: A bright lamp over the chair
A slurpy straw that sucks up water
A chair that tips back slowly
honestyNotes: May feel a little pinch, press or tickle. Never promise 'no pain'. Never threaten with the dentist or mention needles unless the parent did.

fallbackAnswer: It might feel like a little press or a tickle, and it is quick.
If anything feels uncomfortable, you can raise your hand and the dentist will stop and listen.
Yes, [[GROWNUP]] will be right there with you.
You can look at [[GROWNUP]] or hold a hand the whole time.
The little mirror helps the dentist see the back of your teeth.
The tiny brush cleans, and the straw slurps up water. Each tool has one small job.

questionButtons.text: Who will look at my teeth?
fallbackAnswer: A friendly dentist and a helper called a hygienist.
They look at teeth every day and they like to say hello first.
Some tools buzz or whoosh, like a little vacuum cleaner.
The sound is loud, but it is just a tool working. Sunglasses or a toy can help.

techniques.label: Hold a hand or a foot
techniques.how: The parent holds the child's hand or foot during the check-up.

techniques.label: Count the teeth
techniques.how: Count along with the dentist, out loud before and in the head during.

techniques.label: Sunglasses for the lamp
techniques.how: Bring the child's own sunglasses for the bright lamp.

techniques.label: Pick a sticker after
techniques.how: Talk about choosing a sticker at the end, as the 'then' after the 'first'.

techniques.label: Raise a hand to pause
techniques.how: Agree with the dentist that a raised hand means a short break.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose, out slowly through the mouth, three times.

pain: It might feel like a little press or a tickle. If it feels uncomfortable, raise your hand.
Let's practise raising your hand to say 'pause'.
separation: I'll be right here. You can see me the whole time.
Do you want to hold my hand or my finger?
unknown: First we sit in the chair, then the dentist counts your teeth, then you pick a sticker.
Shall we play dentist and practise?
strangers: The dentist is a helper. Let's say hello together.
sensory: The light is bright. Want to wear your sunglasses?
That buzzing is just a tool doing its job.
safety: The dentist's job is to keep your teeth healthy and strong.
love: I'm proud of you for trying something new.

sentences.text: Soon [[CHILD]] is going to visit the dentist.
A dentist is a helper whose job is to keep teeth strong and shiny.
First, [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] walk through the clinic door.
Then they sit in the waiting room, where there are books and sometimes a fish tank.
Waiting is a good time to take slow, big breaths.
When it is [[CHILD]]'s turn, a friendly helper calls out a name.
The dentist chair is big and soft, and it can go up and down like a slow ride.
A bright lamp shines on [[CHILD]]'s teeth so the dentist can see.
The dentist counts every tooth, one by one.
[[CHILD]] can count along in their head.
At the dentist there are a few new grown-ups.
A person at the front desk says hello and writes [[CHILD]]'s name.
A dental helper, called a hygienist, cleans and polishes teeth.
The dentist looks at every tooth and says how strong they are.
It is fine to say hello quietly or just wave.
The helpers wear gloves and sometimes a mask, so their faces look a little different.
Under the mask they are smiling.
[[GROWNUP]] stays close by the whole time.
[[CHILD]] can see [[GROWNUP]] or hold a hand.
If [[CHILD]] wants [[GROWNUP]], [[CHILD]] can say so.
[[CHILD]] has a job at the dentist too.
The job is to sit in the big chair and open wide, like a lion yawning.
The dentist uses a tiny mirror to peek at the back teeth.
A little brush can tickle, and a small straw sucks up water with a slurpy sound.
[[CHILD]] can practise a big lion yawn tonight.
Some tools make buzzing or whooshing sounds.
The sounds are loud, but they are just tools doing their work.
The polish may taste like fruit or mint.
When the dentist says done, [[CHILD]] can close and wiggle the jaw.
Sunglasses can help if the lamp feels too bright.
Sometimes a body feels wobbly or worried before a new thing.
That is okay, and lots of children feel that way.
A check-up may feel like a little pinch, a press or a tickle.
It is usually quick.
If something feels uncomfortable, [[CHILD]] can raise a hand, and the dentist will stop and listen.
When [[CHILD]] feels worried, there are things that help.
[[CHILD]] can squeeze [[GROWNUP]]'s hand or wiggle toes.
[[CHILD]] can breathe in slowly, like smelling a flower, and breathe out, like blowing a candle.
Feelings come and go like clouds.
[[GROWNUP]] is right there.
Tonight [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] can play dentist at home.
[[GROWNUP]] can be the dentist and [[CHILD]] sits in the big chair.
Open wide like a lion and count the teeth together.
Then swap, and [[CHILD]] can be the dentist with a toothbrush.
Practising makes the real visit feel familiar.
After the check-up, [[CHILD]] can pick a sticker.
The dentist may say, Great job keeping your mouth open!
Then [[CHILD]] and [[GROWNUP]] walk out the door together.
[[CHILD]] did something new and brave.
Tomorrow [[CHILD]] can tell someone all about it.
Soon I am going to the dentist.
A dentist is a person who checks teeth.
First, I walk into the clinic with my grown-up.
Then I sit in the waiting room.
There may be books or toys there.
I can wait and take slow breaths.
A helper calls my name when it is my turn.
I go into a room with a big chair.
The chair can move up and down.
A bright lamp shines on my mouth.
The dentist looks at my teeth and counts them.
I can count along in my head.
At the dentist there are new people.
A person at the desk says hello.
A dental hygienist cleans teeth.
The dentist checks teeth.
Many children visit the dentist.
I can say hello or wave.
The helpers wear gloves and sometimes masks.
Masks keep germs away.
My grown-up stays in the room or close by.
I can see my grown-up.
Most children feel safer when they know who is there.
I can ask to hold a hand.
My job is to sit in the chair.
The dentist asks me to open my mouth wide.
The dentist uses a small mirror to see my teeth.
A little brush cleans my teeth.
A small straw takes away water.
I can try to keep my mouth open.
Some tools make buzzing sounds.
The sounds can be loud.
The toothpaste may taste like mint or fruit.
The light can be bright.
When the dentist is finished, I can close my mouth.
I can wear sunglasses if the light is too bright.
Sometimes children feel worried at the dentist.
Feeling worried is okay.
A check-up can feel like pressing or a little pinch.
It usually does not take long.
The dentist wants to help my teeth.
I can raise my hand if I need a break.
My grown-up knows ways to help me.
Many children squeeze a hand or wiggle their toes.
Slow breathing helps many people feel calm.
My grown-up stays near me.
The visit ends and we go home.
I can breathe in slowly and breathe out slowly.
At home I can practise going to the dentist.
My grown-up can pretend to be the dentist.
I sit in a chair and open my mouth wide.
We count my teeth together.
Then we can swap places.
I can practise opening wide.
After the check-up I may get a sticker.
The dentist may say I did a good job.
Then I go home with my grown-up.
I went to the dentist and tried something new.
My grown-up is proud of me.
I can tell someone about my visit.
